elena: quick question — Acme Fin POC wants the Dedicated endpoint locked down. They asked us to provide a list of IPs they can whitelist on their firewall so only their app can call our dedicated route. Also they want us to reach back to their internal S3-like storage for model artifacts; they asked what egress IPs we’ll use for outbound connections. timeline: POC needs network allowlist by EOW.

mike: we can do both but need to clarify two separate flows: 1) inbound allowlist (customer whitelists Redwood source IPs so only we can call their internal services) vs 2) client-side allowlist (customer only allows requests from their app IPs to our dedicated endpoint). which one do they mean?

elena: sorry — they want to both: their infra team will only accept incoming webhooks from Redwood (so they need our egress IPs) and at the same time they want our dedicated endpoint to only accept calls originating from their fixed egress IP range.

mike: cool. short answer: Dedicated pools can be provisioned with stable NAT IPs for outbound connections (so we can give you a stable list to hand to their firewall team). For inbound restriction on our side we support per-credential IP allowlists — we can restrict the API key to only accept requests from their public egress IPs.

kevin: security note: the per-credential IP allowlist plus short-lived POC API keys is the recommended pattern. do NOT share long-lived production keys. also for outbound to customer internal endpoints we recommend TLS mutual auth only if they require mTLS; otherwise standard HTTPS with client certs is not needed. record the IPs and CIDRs we give them in their SCV/SSQ response.

mike: operational details: we can provide either a small set of stable public IPv4 addresses (e.g. 4 IPs) or a /29 for larger needs. typical ports: 443 outbound for HTTPS. avoid opening arbitrary ports — we only use TCP/443 for these flows. sample whitelist entry for their firewall: `ALLOW from 52.23.190.12/32 to <their-host>:443` (we'll give you the exact numbers after pool assignment).

mike: steps we'll take: 1) provision a temporary dedicated pool for the POC, 2) assign stable NAT egress IPs and publish them to you, 3) create a POC-scoped API key with IP allowlist bound to the customer's public IPs, 4) run connectivity test and share curl example and results.

deploy-bot: Dedicated pool "poc-acme-01" created by mike at 2024-11-22T14:04:02Z — pool id dp-87a2

mike: they also asked about DNS and SNI — we use SNI and standard certs. If they want us to reach internal hosts by private hostname they must provide routable host/IPs accessible from our egress path or set up a private peering/VPN (note: private peering is only available on Private deployments or Dedicated with VPC peering addon).

elena: good. they gave us two public egress IPs from their NAT: `198.51.100.34/32` and `198.51.100.35/32`. they asked how to test once we hand over our IPs.

mike: final checklist for network team: 1) exchange CIDRs (we -> them for outbound, they -> us for inbound) 2) they apply their firewall rules to allow our egress IPs to their webhook/S3 endpoints on 443 3) we create POC API key and configure it with their allowed source IPs 4) schedule a 30m validation window and run these tests:
```
# example inbound call test (from their side to our dedicated endpoint)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-Acme123" \
  https://dedicated.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
and for our outbound test to their S3 endpoint we will run an object HEAD to confirm connectivity.

kevin: also capture network ACLs and timestamp tests in the security questionnaire. set key TTL to 72h for the POC and rotate after successful onboarding. if they require IP allowlist changes later, we’ll have a ticket process.

tara: I'll draft the email to their network ops with exact IPs and the steps. ETA: send by EOD. can someone confirm the egress IPs we will publish?

mike: publishing now — egress IPs for dp-87a2: `52.23.190.12/32`, `52.23.190.13/32`, `52.23.190.14/32`, `52.23.190.15/32`. attached to this pool only, not shared with other tenants.

elena: perfect. I'll send the network ops note and loop in their security team. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: once they confirm firewall rules, ping me and I'll run the validation tests.

deploy-bot: API key sk-poc-Acme123 created (expires 72h) for pool dp-87a2 — created by mike at 2024-11-22T14:09:30Z
